newsitem.title: CANADA: Stuttgart talks on Zaire set for Friday - envoy.
newsitem.headline: Stuttgart talks on Zaire set for Friday - envoy.

text.p: A military planning meeting in Stuttgart on the eastern Zaire refugee situation has been set for Friday, the U.N.'s Canadian envoy for the crisis said on Wednesday.

Ambassador Raymond Chretien said the multinational force commander, Lt. Gen. Maurice Baril, would have to evaluate the constantly changing picture. "Gen. Baril and his military commanders on Friday...in Stuttgart will have to take all those new elements, see what will happen on the ground in the next two days and take it from there," he said.

Chretien, nephew of Prime Minister Jean Chretien, was speaking to the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation from Central Africa, where he has been urging Rwanda to facilitate international aid to refugees left in neighboring Zaire.

He said his information was that some refugees in the Bukavu area of Zaire -- where aid agencies say hundreds of thousands of refugees appear to be left -- had begun to return, after at least 500,000 crossed from Goma to the north.

"I'm told that today and tomorrow you can see a few tens of thousands more getting back into Rwanda, especially from the region of Bukavu in eastern Zaire," he said. "The more refugees coming into Rwanda, of course the less need for a strong military intervention."
But he said that at least 400,000 to 500,000 refugees or displaced people were probably left in eastern Zaire.
